- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Eski Mosque was funded by an Ottoman governor and served as a symbol of Ottoman power and influence in the city.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Austro-Hungarian architecture was often associated with the urban elite, who had access to the capital and resources necessary to build grand buildings.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Prefecture building served as a symbol of local authorities' power and authority over the city.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Ottoman-style buildings became part of Craiova's cultural heritage and contributed to the city's diversity.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Austro-Hungarian architecture helped transform Craiova into an important urban center, providing resources and infrastructure for the city's residents.
